panels.title: Macs down
panels.description: `or vector(0)` so the tile reads 0 rather than 'No data' when every Mac is up — an empty tile and a healthy fleet must not look alike.

panels.title: Busiest memory

targets.expr: max(100 * sum by (instance) ({__name__=~"node_memory_(active|wired|compressed)_bytes", job="macos", instance=~"$instance"}) / sum by (instance) (node_memory_total_bytes{job="macos", instance=~"$instance"}))

panels.description: Wired + app + compressed over hw.memsize, i.e. what Activity Monitor calls Memory Used. inactive and purgeable pages are reclaimable and are not counted.

panels.title: Collectors failing
panels.description: A collector that errors makes its panels go quiet while `up` stays 1 — the scrape succeeded, it just carried less. node_exporter reports this per collector itself.

panels.title: CPU time by mode
panels.description: Averaged over cores, so the stack tops out at 1 whatever the core count. macOS reports user, system and nice; there is no iowait or steal on darwin.

panels.title: Load per core

targets.expr: node_load1{job="macos", instance=~"$instance"} / on (instance) group_left () count by (instance) (count by (instance, cpu) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="macos", instance=~"$instance"}))

panels.description: load1 divided by the core count, so a 10-core M-series Mac and a 4-core Intel one are comparable. Above 1 means work is queuing.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (instance) ({__name__=~"node_memory_(active|wired|compressed)_bytes", job="macos", instance=~"$instance"}) / sum by (instance) (node_memory_total_bytes{job="macos", instance=~"$instance"})

panels.title: Memory breakdown
panels.description: Stacks to hw.memsize on one Mac. Compressed growing while free stays flat is macOS absorbing pressure before it starts swapping.

panels.title: Swap used
panels.description: From vm.swapusage. macOS grows its swap files on demand, so total rising is itself a sign of pressure.

panels.title: Page-ins / page-outs
panels.description: darwin's vm_stat pageins/pageouts, which cover file-backed paging too, not only swap — sustained page-outs are the ones that mean trouble.

panels.title: Volume used %
panels.description: On APFS, / and /System/Volumes/Data share one container and report the same numbers: / is the read-only system snapshot. /Volumes/Docker is the external disk Docker Desktop's disk image lives on.

panels.title: Purgeable space
panels.description: APFS space macOS will reclaim under pressure — Finder counts it as free, avail_bytes does not. A volume that looks full with a large purgeable figure is not actually out of room.

panels.title: Errors and drops / s

targets.expr: sum by (instance, device) (rate({__name__=~"node_network_(receive|transmit)_(errors|errs)_total", job="macos", instance=~"$instance", device=~"en[0-9]+|bridge[0-9]+"}[5m]))
sum by (instance, device) (rate({__name__=~"node_network_(receive|transmit)_(dropped|drop)_total", job="macos", instance=~"$instance", device=~"en[0-9]+|bridge[0-9]+"}[5m]))

panels.description: darwin spells these node_network_receive_errors_total and node_network_receive_dropped_total, where Linux says _errs_ and _drop_ — a copied-from-Linux panel silently charts nothing here, so both spellings are matched. darwin has no transmit-dropped counter at all.

panels.title: GPU busy %
panels.description: IOKit's Device Utilization for each accelerator, sampled by scripts/macos-gpu-textfile.sh and served through node_exporter's textfile collector — node_exporter's darwin build has no GPU collector of its own, so a Mac that is up with no series here has not had scripts/install-macos-gpu-exporter.sh run on it.

panels.title: GPU memory
panels.description: On Apple silicon this is unified memory the GPU holds, so it is already counted in the Memory panels above rather than being extra RAM. Allocated is the reservation, in use is the live part of it.

panels.title: Renderer and tiler utilization
panels.description: The two engines behind the overall busy figure. The tiler series is Apple silicon only — an Intel or AMD GPU reports no tiler, and an empty half here is the expected reading on those Macs, not a broken sampler.

panels.title: GPU busy % (now)
panels.description: Each GPU's latest sample. This is a point sample taken every 15s, not an average over the scrape interval like the CPU panels, so a short burst can fall between two samples and never appear.

panels.title: GPUs
panels.description: model is empty on Intel Macs: the IOKit property holds raw hex there rather than a readable name, and is left undecoded. If a Mac vanishes from this table while up{job="macos"} is still 1, its sampler agent has stopped — check time() - node_textfile_mtime_seconds{job="macos"}.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: A Mac that keeps reappearing with minutes of uptime is rebooting — or waking from a sleep long enough to have dropped out of the scrape, which `up` alone reports as a flapping target.

panels.title: Macs
panels.description: `release` is the Darwin kernel version, not the macOS marketing one (Darwin 24.x is macOS 15): node_exporter exposes no metric for the latter. `machine` is arm64 on Apple Silicon.

panels.title: Battery charge %
panels.description: Laptops only — a Mac mini or Studio has no power source to report and stays empty here. Needs the powersupplyclass collector, which is on by default on darwin.

panels.title: Battery time remaining
panels.description: IOKit reports -1 while charging or while it is still estimating, so `> 0` drops those rather than charting a negative duration.

panels.title: Power source and battery health
panels.description: The state label is the one currently true: AC Power or Battery Power. `== 1` keeps that row and drops the other enum values, which are exported as 0.
